title: A little more depth, a little less repetition
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Light and sound
items: Rebalanced sunlight, cool sky fill and moonlight across the garden, village and main menu, with longer-range shadows and stronger contact shading.
Ground normal maps and imported material roughness retain more detail. Rain darkens and changes the sheen of exposed model surfaces while dry ground stays matte.
Start-menu Options now has Master, Music, UI, Ambience, Sound Effects and Speech controls, saved independently. Zero mutes the chosen category; music fades and dialogue ducking still work.

sections.heading: Arthur and Valley Club
items: Arthur’s welcome now plays once per release, rather than every garden entry or village return. Heard welcomes are remembered locally per account and travel with the garden save; the next published version welcomes you again.
Valley Club checks for a newer cloud save every 30 seconds while visible and when you return to the page. It keeps the last loaded garden if a request fails and retries automatically.
Expired watering entries no longer inflate watered-tile counts. Gardening activity is labelled as recorded actions rather than incorrectly claiming an older day’s actions happened today.
Existing gardens and audio preferences remain compatible. Club updates still depend on a successful game upload or five-minute autosave; this does not change the cloud conflict safeguards.

intro: Arthur has discovered the release number. This is excellent news for anyone who has heard his welcome speech three times while popping out for a chicken. Meanwhile, the valley has acquired a little more shadow, and the sound desk now has enough faders to make the watering can feel like a recording artist.
why: Bright ambient fill was flattening the garden. A stronger directional light, quieter sky fill, contact shading and more visible surface normals help rocks, soil and characters read as solid objects. Rain now catches exposed surfaces differently from sheltered sides.
Six volume controls mean Arthur can remain audible while the music takes a polite step back. Existing quiet interface sounds, scene fades and saved preferences are preserved.
A welcome belongs to an arrival, not every shopping trip. The build records its release version, and completed greetings are remembered across reloads and cloud saves.

The Club was waiting for someone to press Refresh. It now checks quietly for a newer cloud snapshot, shows its saved date and revision, and retries a failed check without throwing away the last garden. Expired watering marks also stop posing as freshly watered soil.
issues: The website displays cloud snapshots, not a live feed. New gardening work appears after a successful manual upload or the existing five-minute autosave, then the next website refresh.

Game checks cover category routing, mute and persistence, welcome history and save compatibility. Isolated browser tests use fixture accounts to verify refresh, retry, weather, balances and terrain statistics; no live player account was changed.
These notes describe the local development update. The game and website changes reach players when the next version is manually published.

screenshots.caption: The start-menu sound mixer, with six independent volume controls and a Back button that stays visible.
A local test garden showing the revised daylight, textured ground and distant landscape. The save used for testing is separate from player gardens.

title: Little sounds, with room for the birds
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Quiet interface feedback
items: Added native UI SFX feedback for menus, tools, field-guide navigation, confirmed purchases, invalid placement, resident movement and visible wildlife notices.
Organic is the quiet default; all 12 sound styles are available in Options, with a separate interface volume, mute switch and optional typing sounds.
Login and manual cloud-upload feedback follows the actual result. Background refreshes, routine autosaves, hover and password typing remain silent.
Repeated notifications and volume adjustments are limited, typing is not rate-limited, and mute stops interface sounds immediately. Existing music, ambience and visible feedback remain in place.

intro: The buttons have found their voices. Fortunately, they have agreed to use their indoor voices. A purchase gets a little acknowledgement, a menu has a gentle rustle, and the birds do not have to compete with a fanfare every time someone considers a watering can.
why: We reviewed all twelve UI SFX styles and chose Organic for its wood-and-water character. It suits the garden, while a style selector leaves the other eleven available for anyone whose chicken prefers science fiction.
Sounds mark actual events: a paid purchase, a confirmed move, a successful sign-in or an upload that really finished. Hovering and routine background work stay quiet.

Mute, interface volume and optional typing sounds are saved separately from the master volume. Typing is off by default, password fields stay silent, and existing visual feedback still carries every message.
issues: These are native Godot audio files, not a browser audio dependency. No repeating UI loops were added over the existing loading music or valley ambience.
Automated checks cover mute persistence, input gating, duplicate suppression, account outcomes and purchase/movement cues. Physical controller listening balance remains a hands-on check.
Audio assets are from UI SFX 0.4.0 under CC0, with source and licence information included.

screenshots.caption: Local development build: interface volume, all twelve sound styles, mute and optional typing controls in Options.

title: Check the paperwork before packing the valley
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: More reliable manual publishing
items: Release notes and blog images are now checked before building the game or contacting GitHub, avoiding a completed build followed by a missing-notes failure.
Empty or placeholder release notes produce a clear explanation of what to fix, without a Python traceback. Interrupted releases with already-promoted notes can still resume.
A read-only publishing check is available for future updates. Existing game saves and gameplay are unchanged.

intro: The publisher used to pack the whole valley into a suitcase, zip it shut, and only then ask whether anyone had written the label. We have moved the paperwork to the beginning. The hedgehog remains opposed to being checked luggage.
why: A missing changelog should be discovered before the slow build and compression work. Release notes, their title and the blog images are now checked first.
The error now points to the notes that need attention. A retry after notes were already promoted still works, so recovering an interrupted release does not require inventing another update.
issues: This fixes the release-preparation failure shown in the report. Authentication, network outages and unrelated build failures can still stop a release; they are separate checks.
This update changes publishing tools only. Existing garden saves need no migration.

title: A place for everything, including the chicken
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Place purchases in your garden
items: Shop purchases now return you to the garden with a translucent preview. Choose clear, dry ground and rotate with LB/RB (L1/R1), or Q/E on keyboard.
Confirm with A / Cross or left click. B / Circle or Escape cancels without spending coins; payment happens only after a valid placement is saved.
Placed objects keep their rotation, and purchased animals keep their latest garden position in saves. Older saves remain compatible.

sections.heading: Guide your residents
items: Aim at a resident animal and press A / Cross (R on keyboard) to choose its destination. A gold ring stays with the waiting animal while a blue ring selects the destination.
Confirm to let the animal walk around blocked ground; cancel to let it wander again. Player two uses yellow and red markers, with separate placement ownership.
Xbox X / PlayStation Square now opens the tool wheel. A / Cross remains the selection and confirmation button; shovel modes are available inside the wheel.

sections.heading: Clear saving feedback
items: The save emblem spins for at least four seconds for a save, and remains visible if a cloud upload takes longer. Local and cloud result messages still report the actual outcome.
Reviewed all 13 published studio posts, including the corrected v0.1.19 follow-up and v0.1.23 loading-screen story. Added a repeatable local audit for release details, authors, links and images.

intro: Buying a bench used to be an act of faith: hand over the coins and hope the delivery service shared your artistic vision. Now the bench auditions as a slightly ghostly bench first. The chicken has also acquired a very small traffic-control system.
why: The garden is yours to arrange. A translucent preview lets you judge position and rotation before spending anything, while occupied ground, water and steep patches explain why a spot is unsuitable. Cancelling leaves the purse untouched.

A resident should be easy to guide without being teleported across the flowerbeds. One colour stays with the waiting animal and the other marks its destination; after confirmation it walks there, then resumes its usual important investigations. Each split-screen spirit has its own interaction.

X / Square opens tools so A / Cross can handle selection. The save emblem now takes a four-second turn even when a local save is quick. A longer cloud upload keeps it visible; a reassuring spin does not turn a failed upload into a successful one.
issues: Placement needs clear, dry ground inside the garden and rejects uneven footprints. Animals need a reachable dry destination; visitors must become residents before they can be guided.
An animal pauses at its chosen destination, then returns to wandering. This is a gentle move request, not a permanent stay command.
Controller interactions have automated coverage for both players, including cancellation and ownership. Physical Xbox and PlayStation hardware still needs a hands-on check.
Old saves remain compatible. New purchase records include rotation; purchased animals update their saved position when the garden saves.

screenshots.caption: Local development build: a gold marker stays with the waiting chicken while the blue marker chooses where it will walk.

title: A proper welcome, and a little sign of saving
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Welcome back
items: A personalised welcome popup greets you by username after sign-in, including remembered sessions.
Press A / Cross, Enter or Head Outside to continue to the garden, or stay at the main menu.
The popup explains autosave and shows the supplied save icon; it also flags any unresolved cloud-garden choice.

sections.heading: Saving and account access
items: The new save emblem rotates slowly during local autosaves and cloud uploads. Local and cloud results remain separate toast messages.
In-game Sign In and Create Account now use separate forms. Existing players need only their email and password to sign in.
Verified protected login restoration, sign-out cleanup, five-minute autosaves and garden/village account badges.

intro: The valley now remembers your name and says hello before handing you a hoe. There is also a small rotating mountain-and-floppy-disk badge, because even a peaceful garden occasionally needs to say: one moment, I am writing this down.
why: The welcome explains saving before you start playing, using your username and the supplied save artwork. Controller players get the matching A or Cross prompt.
The save icon stays visible through cloud uploads, while the toast tells you whether the garden reached the cloud or was saved locally.
Sign-in and registration are now separate inside the game as well as on the website. Existing gardeners need not wade through new-account fields.
issues: Cloud conflicts still need a garden choice in Account & Cloud. The welcome makes that clear rather than silently replacing either save.
Windows protects remembered refresh sessions; revoked sessions still require signing in again. Passwords are not saved.
Tests use disposable player profiles and fixture accounts. Screenshot usernames are examples, not real player data.

screenshots.caption: Development build with a test username: the welcome popup and supplied save icon.
Development build: registration has its own in-game form.

title: A louder pause and a left-turning rabbit
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Small valley adjustments
items: Raised Pause and Look by 6 dB so the pause-menu music is easier to hear.
Rotated the arrival rabbit 90 degrees to the left.

intro: The pause music has found its voice, and the rabbit has received a very specific direction: left. Not a grand expedition, just ninety degrees.
why: Pause and Look was too quiet, so its level is now 6 dB higher in both garden and village pauses.
The arrival rabbit needed its model facing turned another quarter-turn to the left.
issues: These are volume and model-orientation adjustments; existing saves remain compatible.

title: The front door now opens
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Website account access
items: Fixed publishing omitting a required website module, which prevented the account script and sign-in buttons from starting.
Sign in and Create account now have separate forms. Existing players sign in with their game email and password; usernames are requested during registration.
Added a clear message if account files fail to load. Profile or garden service errors no longer look like failed sign-in.
Website publishing now includes local JavaScript dependencies automatically and checks for missing files before uploading.

intro: We built a lovely Valley Club front door and then forgot to deliver one of its hinges. The game could sign in perfectly well; the published website was missing a JavaScript module and stood there looking decorative. This update brings the hinge.
why: Sign-in and registration deserve separate forms. Existing gardeners should not have to stare at a username box meant for new arrivals.
The publisher now follows website module dependencies automatically, so adding a new statistics helper cannot quietly strand the account page.
A successful login now stays visibly successful even if a garden or profile service needs a retry.
issues: Confirmed the deployed garden-metrics.js returned 404 while club.html and club.js returned 200. The fix is local until the next manual website publication.

Local browser checks cover separate registration and sign-in, bad passwords, profile-service failures, missing startup files and the existing friends flow. No real player password or account was used.

screenshots.caption: Local preview: existing players sign in with email and password, without registration fields.
Local preview: a separate registration form collects a unique username and account details.

title: Good neighbours, little portraits and a proper pause
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Your Valley Club identity
items: New accounts choose a unique username; existing players can claim one while keeping their garden.
Every profile receives a generated valley portrait, stored with the account and shown on the website.

sections.heading: Neighbours and garden notebooks
items: Search usernames, send and accept friend requests, decline or cancel invitations, and remove friends.
Compare accepted friends’ latest uploaded gardens across money, experience, wildlife, gardening, land coverage and more. Full saves remain private.
Open your own garden notebook for all recorded statistics.

sections.heading: A quieter pause
items: Pause and Look plays softly when the garden or village is paused; regular music resumes when play continues.

sections.heading: Service setup
items: Requires the new Valley Club Supabase migration and the matching game and website. Existing saves remain compatible.

intro: The valley has acquired neighbours. Naturally, we gave everyone a tiny mountain portrait and the ability to discover whose garden contains the most suspiciously deliberate hard dirt.
why: Unique usernames make gardeners easier to find than email addresses. Automatic portraits give each account an identity without another upload form.
Mutual requests keep comparisons between willing neighbours. A notebook collects the numbers without turning the front page into an agricultural tax return.
Pause and Look gives a pause its own soundtrack. The hoe can wait.
issues: The Supabase migration has been applied. Live checks confirm username validation works and signed-out callers cannot read profiles, friendships or the directory. Authenticated signup and friendship flows were tested locally with isolated data; no live accounts were created.
Comparisons reflect uploaded saves and are not cheat-proof rankings. Missing measurements appear as unavailable.
Usernames are permanent in this version. Existing players need to claim one; old game clients must update before registering.

screenshots.caption: Local website preview with test accounts: generated portraits, friends and garden comparisons.

title: A soundtrack for the valley, and a save that travels
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Cloud saves and loading
items: Fixed local saves being uploaded with a decimal-format version number that the existing cloud server rejected.
Kept the clock from drawing before the day/night cycle is ready during garden loading.
The loading reveal now uses a prepared camera, avoiding a brief incorrect split-screen view before the arrival walk.

sections.heading: Music through the day
items: Morning in the Vale accompanies the first walk into the garden.
Morning and afternoon each have a pool of suitable tracks; shuffle bags play every eligible track before refilling and avoid an immediate repeat when possible.
Twilight Pastoral accompanies evening and night, with a lower night-time volume.
Music stays soft, fades between time periods, ducks during Arthur’s dialogue and pauses on the main menu or while loading. Garden and village share one soundtrack.

sections.heading: Studio journal
items: Replaced the v0.1.23 placeholder post with its loading-screen story and corrected v0.1.19’s outdated unreleased follow-up wording.

intro: The cloud save was wearing a decimal point where its identity badge should have been. That is now corrected. Meanwhile, the valley has acquired a soundtrack: morning optimism, afternoon wandering and twilight politely asking everyone to lower their voices.
why: The server accepted save format 1, but reading a local JSON file turned it into 1.0 on the next upload. Both describe the same version, yet the existing server compared their text. The client now sends the expected integer without changing anyone’s garden.

The new tracks are selected using the garden clock. Morning in the Vale also accompanies the arrival walk; the afternoon tracks share a shuffled pool with Beautiful Day, and Twilight Pastoral keeps evening and night gentle.
A shared soundtrack follows the garden into the village. It fades down for Arthur, pauses during loading, and avoids playing the same track twice in succession when another suitable one is available.
The v0.1.23 post no longer claims there was nothing to report while a shower of daffodils was clearly happening. The v0.1.19 follow-up now acknowledges that its scenery changes shipped in v0.1.20.
issues: The upload regression was reproduced locally and its outgoing request format is now tested. A successful retry on the player’s authenticated live account has not yet been verified.
Music scheduling, shuffling and dialogue ducking are tested in code. Twilight Pastoral currently serves both evening and night because no separate night track was supplied.

screenshots.caption: Development build: daffodils reveal the prepared arrival camera before the walk begins.

title: A few petals while the valley wakes
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Loading the garden
items: Added a dark six-petal loading animation inspired by the supplied video, with short messages describing garden preparation.
I Will Wait plays while the garden loads and fades out as soon as it is ready; the game does not wait for the track to finish.
Copies of the supplied Border-1 daffodil artwork scatter across the screen to reveal the garden.
Moved scene-resource loading into a background request and added preparation checkpoints before the arrival walk or Arthur’s welcome begins.

intro: The valley now has something to do while it finds its boots. Six blue petals light up in the dark, I Will Wait keeps them company, and a small blizzard of daffodils announces that your garden is ready. The song title is a suggestion, not a demand.
why: Loading is part of the first impression. The supplied video gave us a clear starting point: a quiet dark background and six petals waking in blue, recreated as a procedural animation that can keep looping for as long as preparation takes.
Music should make waiting pleasant without becoming the reason you are still waiting. Readiness triggers a brief fade and flower scatter, regardless of where the song has reached.
The first-arrival walk and welcome dialogue begin after the reveal, so their opening moments are not hidden behind a loading screen.
issues: The animation is inspired by the video rather than playing the video file itself. Each individual preparation step still runs on the game thread and can briefly hold a frame.
A clock redraw could run before its day/night cycle existed during staged setup. A guard for this is included in the following development update.

screenshots.caption: The six-petal loading screen introduced in v0.1.23, captured in the local development build.

update_note: Replaced placeholder copy with the actual v0.1.23 release contents.

title: One valley, one studio, fewer keyboards
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Website and studio identity
items: Matched the main website, blog and changelog to the Valley Club palette, typography and cards, with a direct club invitation on the homepage.
Corrected the studio name to Waldas Game Studios across website credits and blog bylines.
Added the supplied WGS logo to website footers and the game main menu.

sections.heading: Controller text entry
items: Added an on-screen keyboard for editable text fields when using a controller, including account email/password and developer-console input.
Use the D-pad or left stick to move, A / Cross to select, B / Circle to cancel, X / Square to delete, Y / Triangle to change case, and Start / Options to finish.
Includes symbols, spaces, password masking and physical keyboard support. Cancel leaves the original field unchanged and closes without retaining its draft.

intro: The website and the Valley Club have finally agreed on the curtains. Forest green, parchment and a little gold won the vote. Waldas Game Studios also has its correct name on the door, and a controller can now write an email address without demanding a second piece of furniture.
why: The homepage should feel like the same place as your private garden dashboard. Shared colours, cards and studio branding connect the download page, journal and club without changing what each page is there to do.
The supplied WGS artwork now signs the website and main menu. The studio-name correction also applies to earlier blog bylines; the historical release stories themselves are unchanged.

Signing in from a sofa needs proper text entry. The on-screen keyboard has controller navigation, symbols, case switching and explicit Done and Cancel actions. Password drafts remain masked and are cleared when the keyboard closes.
issues: Controller events were tested programmatically in Godot, including typing, deletion, cancellation, focus return and password masking. Physical Xbox and PlayStation hardware have not been tested in this update.
Desktop and mobile layouts passed local browser checks. These changes are not published until the next manual release.

screenshots.caption: Local development preview: the homepage adopts the Valley Club visual style.
Development build: controller text entry on the account screen.

title: A home for your garden, wherever you play
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Garden fixes
items: Both players begin with no tool equipped.
Turned the arrival rabbit to face its direction of travel.

sections.heading: Accounts and cloud-save integration
items: Added an Account & Cloud screen with email registration, sign-in, password-reset requests and sign-out.
Added explicit local/cloud garden selection, automatic syncing after local saves, revision-conflict protection and local backups before cloud downloads. Offline play remains available.
Added a private Your Valley website dashboard showing uploaded coins, animal population, XP, land coverage and wildlife visit/residency dates.

Supabase database setup is installed and signed-out access is denied. Redirect URLs are configured; public account launch still needs email delivery, live authenticated acceptance checks and manual publication.

intro: The rabbit has stopped attempting a moonwalk, and your spirit now arrives without immediately brandishing a hoe. Meanwhile, the valley is getting cloud saves. These clouds have considerably better filing cabinets than the ones Arthur complains about.
why: Starting with empty hands gives the first arrival room to breathe. The rabbit correction makes its little crossing read as an actual journey rather than a disagreement with physics.

The new account screen and private Valley Club dashboard let one garden follow its owner across devices. Coins, wildlife and progress belong together; nobody should need a spreadsheet to remember which hedgehog moved in.
Choosing a local or cloud garden is deliberate, and older uploads cannot silently overwrite newer ones. A backup stays on the computer before a cloud download replaces its local save.
issues: The development integration is ready for account testing, but the website and game have not been published. Redirect URLs are configured; a working confirmation and recovery email sender is still required before public registration.
Live checks confirmed that signed-out access is denied. Game save/restore and mocked account/dashboard tests passed; two-account authenticated database and real email delivery tests remain pending.
Sign-in is session-only for now. The dashboard shows the last uploaded snapshot, and cloud conflicts pause syncing until the player chooses how to resolve them.

title: Familiar faces at the garden gate
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Arrival scenery
items: Replaced the crossing placeholder with the supplied rabbit, the flying placeholder with the animated robin, and the distant animals with the supplied bull model.
Added a textured rock outside each garden corner, with varied rotations that stay consistent when reloading.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance for your first arrival and returns to wandering after his welcome.
Reduced the rock’s game mesh detail while preserving its original source model and texture.

sections.heading: Studio notes
items: Updated the latest blog post with the previous Blender robin animation work and a dated development follow-up covering these arrival improvements.

intro: The temporary rabbit has handed in its notice. A proper rabbit has taken the role, the robin has brought its newly animated wings, and the bulls have agreed to stand in the distance looking as though they own the place. Arthur, meanwhile, has finally checked the arrival time.
why: The first arrival established the route and camera timing. Replacing its stand-ins with the supplied models makes those little look-around moments belong to the valley. The flying robin reuses the Blender animation made from the two motion references.

Four rocks give the garden corners a little visual definition without bringing back the perimeter wall. Their varied angles are repeatable, so loading a saved garden does not cause a geological reshuffle.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance until his welcome finishes. Being greeted is rather more welcoming when the greeter has not wandered off halfway through your approach.
issues: The rabbit and bull sources contain rigs but no animation clips. The rabbit currently uses a simple whole-body hop; the bulls have subtle breathing movement. Their full skeletal gait animations are still future work.
These arrival animals are scenery, not purchased livestock or new visitor discoveries. The robin’s separate wildlife visit still needs 1% water.
A missing texture connection on the rock was corrected during import. The original source models and textures remain intact.

title: Taking the scenic route
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: A walk into the valley
items: Added a gravel pathway following the northern mountains and hills down to the garden edge, using the supplied gravel textures.
New gardens now begin with a short downhill camera walk, gentle footstep bobbing and smooth looks toward a crossing creature, passing bird, birch tree and two distant animals.
The arrival leads into Arthur’s welcome. Escape, B / Circle or Start skips the walk; existing gardens receive the path without replaying the arrival.
Time, weather and ambience continue throughout the shared arrival, with normal single-player or split-screen play restored afterwards. The scenery placeholders do not count as wildlife visits.

sections.heading: Previous follow-up: the robin learns its moves
items: Created an editable Blender rig and reference-inspired idle, hopping and flight animations, preserving the source FBX and texture.
Connected the clips to garden movement and short low flights, while retaining the 1% water visit requirement and existing saved discoveries.

sections.heading: Later scenery follow-up — released in v0.1.20
items: Replaced the crossing placeholder with the supplied rabbit, the flying placeholder with the animated robin, and the distant animals with the supplied bull model.
Added a textured rock outside each garden corner, with varied rotations that stay consistent when reloading.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance for your first arrival and returns to wandering after his welcome.

intro: The first walk into the valley gave a new garden a proper arrival: gravel underfoot, a little camera bob and several excellent excuses to look around. This article also records the later robin animation and scenery follow-up, which was released in v0.1.20.
why: A new garden should feel like somewhere you have travelled to. The gravel approach connects the northern mountain scenery to the plot, while a short walk gives the valley a chance to introduce itself before Arthur does.

The camera follows the actual hillside surface, with a small walking bob and eased turns. Four staged moments give the journey a little life: something crosses your path, a bird passes, a birch catches your eye, and two animals stand further away.

Early captures showed grass growing through the new gravel. Admirable botanical enthusiasm, but rather poor path maintenance. We cleared the route and moved nearby tree placements back so the approach reads more clearly.

The robin follow-up gave the previously unrigged bird an 11-bone Blender rig with idle, hopping and flight clips, inspired by the supplied motion videos. Its wings can now do the work instead of relying on a whole-model bounce. No tiny pilot licence was required.

Later follow-up, released in v0.1.20: the real rabbit, animated robin and bulls replace the arrival stand-ins; varied corner rocks define the plot, and Arthur waits at the entrance. These scene changes were subsequently released in v0.1.20.
issues: The original arrival used deliberately simple stand-ins. The development follow-up replaces their appearances, while keeping them separate from collectible or resident wildlife.
The first robin skin-weight pass pulled some head vertices with a wing. Those weights were corrected before export. The motion is authored from reference, not automatically captured from the videos.
The rabbit and bull files have rigs but no clips: the crossing rabbit currently hops as a whole model and the bulls use gentle breathing motion. Full skeletal gait work is still pending.

The upper mountain route remains scenery. Arrival completion, skipping, Arthur’s waiting state, corner placement and split-screen handover have automated coverage; physical controller testing remains outstanding.

intro: Previously, arriving in the garden involved the traditional Welsh practice of appearing out of thin air. We have now installed a path. The rabbit-shaped object using it has declined to pay council tax.
why: A new garden should feel like somewhere you have travelled to. The gravel approach connects the northern mountain scenery to the plot, while a short walk gives the valley a chance to introduce itself before Arthur does.

title: A little breathing room
author: Waldas Game Studios

sections.heading: Menus and button hints
items: Restored the clean woodland-green garden pause and village shop menus, removing the decorative petal borders.
Button hints now float beside the analogue clock, with outlined text for contrast against the scenery. The daffodil tool wheel and its controller controls stay in place.

sections.heading: Notes from the studio
items: Added a website blog by Waldas Game Studios, with release stories, reasons for changes, recorded issues and development screenshots.
Manual publishing now creates one blog post per new release and includes it in the website update.

intro: The menus had dressed for a flower show. Lovely ambition; rather a lot of elbows at the tea table. We have asked the decorative borders to take the afternoon off and given the valley a little breathing room.
why: The decorative frames made the pause and shop menus feel busier than intended. Following player feedback, those panels return to their simpler woodland-green appearance. The daffodil tool wheel keeps its petals because they are the actual selections, rather than extra decoration.
Button hints now sit directly over the scene. A dark text outline helps them stay readable against bright skies and pale ground, without putting another box between you and the garden.

The changelog tells you what changed. This blog adds the why, the rough edges, and screenshots where we have them. Each manual release now preserves its own studio note, so the story will not quietly turn into next week’s story.
issues: Controller icons follow the device name reported by the driver. A PlayStation controller presented as a virtual Xbox pad will still show Xbox symbols. Hardware-specific behaviour needs checking on real controllers; the automated checks simulate input.
The new menu treatment follows feedback on the last update. Sometimes the most productive gardening tool is an eraser. No saved-garden format changes are needed for this update.
